11.content: Signals connect state to the text and properties that read it. Updates change retained nodes without rerunning the entire component.
11.keywords: signal reactivity memo effect batch cleanup

12.content: @reactive.create_signal(initial) returns (read, write) . A call such as @ui.text("Count: \{count()}") is reactive when built with QuickGUI. The compiler also tracks expressions in button content, native properties, fluent styles, interaction styles, and child lists. Each binding updates its own retained nodes; the component does not rerun. Binding expressions must be pure. Ordinary setup remains ordinary MoonBit: let initial = count() captures a snapshot. Event handlers run only on events. Use @reactive.untrack(count) for an untracked read. Custom components keep normal parameter types: pass a getter when their input should stay live. Explicit bind_* methods and the lower-level Signal handle remain available for manual composition and keyed rows.

13.content: @reactive.memo(() => expression) returns a signal for a derived value. @reactive.create_effect tracks its actual reads, including conditional dependencies. @reactive.batch coalesces related writes. Avoid effects that rebuild an entire view to update one label. Components and dynamic branches own their subscriptions. Register teardown with @reactive.on_cleanup . Removing the owner retires its effects and callbacks; new windows have independent owners.

14.content: Components construct a retained tree once when mounted. Reactive bindings update the affected nodes; the native core handles layout, painting, and accessibility.
14.keywords: rendering retained children mount lifecycle keyed

15.content: Constructors accept only children or content. Empty containers use [] ; buttons also accept a string or one element. Apply styles, properties, and event handlers through fluent methods such as .padding(24) , .checked(checked()) , and .on_click(save) . Use .style(shared) for reusable styles. Read getters directly in fluent properties: @ui.checkbox([]).checked(checked()).on_checked_change(set_checked) . Literal properties initialize component-owned state; expressions containing signal reads become controlled bindings. Styles merge in declaration order. Use child lists throughout; scoped parts can attach a complete list with .children([...]) .

16.content: The branch factory runs when the predicate switches branches. Put values that change within that branch in bindings so its nodes can stay mounted.

17.content: Keys must be unique and stable. The render callback receives a row signal, so existing rows can update without replacing native node IDs or local state. Keyed children alone do not virtualize a long list; use table visible ranges .

18.content: Use quickgui check and quickgui test so tests receive the same view transform as builds. Add --release for release-backend tests. Raw moon check checks the original types, while raw moon test bypasses implicit view bindings. The CLI preserves source files and maps compiler diagnostics, assertion failures, and symbolicated stack locations back to them. Native debugger breakpoints and stepping currently use the generated files in .quickgui/moonbit-sources ; original-file breakpoint mapping is not supported yet. Editor completion and type checking continue to use ordinary MoonBit.

20.content: Declare routes with @ui.route . Use @ui.layout to share surrounding content, and call its outlet() callback where the matched child belongs. Mount the router with router.outlet() .

21.content: Use router.link(path, label) for a navigation link. router.navigate(path) pushes history; pass replace=true to replace the current entry. router.go(-1) goes back and router.go(1) goes forward.

22.content: Outlets retain nodes by matched route identity. Navigating between sibling routes keeps their common layout and its state. Read router.state() in a binding for the current location and matched parameters; router.is_active(path) tests a navigation destination.

23.content: Compose fluent styles, merge declarations, and bind native state styles. Element methods and @ui.style() share the same native style properties. Numeric dimensions are pixels; strings support percentages and native keywords.

24.content: Use .flex_row() , .flex_col() , .items_center() , and .justify_center() for common layouts. .flex(1) sets grow, shrink, and a zero basis. Give scrollable flex children .min_height(0) and a bounded parent size.

25.hierarchy: Styling & Layout › Merging and reactive styles
25.content: .style(base).style(overrides) merges declarations in order; later properties win. .merge(other) does the same for style builders. Applying a style takes a snapshot. Changing the builder later does not update the mounted element. The compiler binds getter reads inside .style(...) and fluent modifiers. Later declarations keep precedence on every update; disappearing declarations are cleared or reveal an earlier fallback. Interaction-style callbacks can also read getters. Mutating an already-applied reusable builder is still a snapshot mutation, so derive styles from signals instead.

26.content: Use .hover(s => ...) , .active(s => ...) , and .focus_style(s => ...) for native pointer and focus states. .selected_style styles selected compound parts. These states are resolved by the native core. For a drop target’s drag-over appearance, use bind_json with @protocol.DRAG_OVER_STYLE and return a style’s .json() . Configure the node as a drop target as well; a style does not enable drop behavior. Import egoist/quickgui/protocol when using protocol constants. Add transitions to the base style to animate state changes.

27.content: Use @ui.rgb8(r, g, b) or @ui.rgba8(r, g, b, a) , with channels from 0 to 255. Window options accept these colors as JSON values; a raw integer uses 0xAABBGGRR ( 0 for transparent). Do not pass CSS color strings as a window’s background . @ui.svg(source) produces a mask tinted by .text_color(...) . For multiple graph colors, use separate tinted SVG layers, as shown in Quick Git.

28.content: Animate retained paint properties without per-frame MoonBit work. Transitions interpolate native style changes on an existing element. Declare a target and timing; the core advances the frames and stops requesting them when complete.
28.keywords: transition animation easing duration transform reduced motion 动画 过渡 アニメーション

29.content: Put timing on the base element so both entering and leaving a state animate. A signal-driven bind_style target uses the same transition. Changing a target mid-transition starts from the current visible value.

30.content: Durations are milliseconds, bounded to 0–10 seconds. .transition_easing(...) accepts linear , ease , ease-in , ease-out , or ease-in-out . .transition_max_fps(30) optionally caps the frame rate; omit it to follow presentation. One element has one duration, easing, and frame-rate cap for its selected properties. Delays and custom cubic Bézier curves are not supported.

31.content: Transition background-color , border-color , border-width , border-radius , color , opacity , box-shadow , and transform . all selects these paint properties. Width, height, padding, gradients, and other layout changes do not interpolate. Use a transform for a sliding thumb instead of animating its layout position. For an animated image, use @ui.image(path) with a GIF or WebP. The native decoder retains frames and repeat policy; no signal timer is needed.

32.hierarchy: Transitions & Animation › Lifetime and reduced motion
32.content: Initial styles apply directly. Keep an element mounted to animate a target change; child_if removes a branch immediately and does not wait for an exit fade. Zero opacity still occupies layout and accepts input. Transitions respect the system Reduce Motion preference. Hidden or occluded windows pause local transitions.

Use platform roles for commands such as closing, hiding, or minimizing a window. Use Dialog , Popover , SystemPopover and Tooltip for their native focus, dismissal and lifetime behavior. 48.content: Manage window lifetimes and asynchronous native work. Call @native.run once. Its startup callback creates windows and registers application services. Results and events run on the MoonBit UI thread.

49.content: Use @ui.window(component, options=...) to create a window; each window owns an independent tree. @native.current_window() is valid while building a component or handling a window callback. Capture that handle for later .close() or .focus() calls. Creation is asynchronous. Wait for window-ready-to-show before querying native geometry or state. Set show: false to prepare a hidden window. Options use the native JSON schema, including title , width , height , background , titleBarStyle , trafficLightX , and trafficLightY .

50.hierarchy: Windows & Native Services › Commands and services
50.content: @native.command(json, callback) sends platform commands. @native.invoke(operation, params, callback) calls an asynchronous native service. Both callbacks receive Result[Json, String] . Use them for operations that need a response. @native.call is restricted to the core’s synchronous CPU-only allowlist. Callbacks belong to their registering owner. If an operation should survive the row or dialog that starts it, register it inside window.with_owner(() => { ... }) . Closing that window still retires the callback.

51.hierarchy: Windows & Native Services › Events and file watching
51.content: @native.on_event(kind, listener) subscribes in the current window context. @native.subscribe also returns a cancellation function. Use window=0 for application-level events. @native.watch_files(paths, changed, ready) uses OS file notifications and returns a stop function. These subscriptions are cleaned up with their owner. Persistent extension events use extension-event ; filter event.target to the session you opened. See Authoring Extensions .

52.content: Package independent native providers and call them from MoonBit. Extensions add optional native services without changing the core. Go and MoonBit share the same manifest and service ABI; each frontend supplies its own public wrapper.
52.keywords: extension authoring provider init-extension rust zig pure go manifest ABI 扩展 拡張

53.content: From the QuickGUI checkout, scaffold a provider: The command accepts moonbit , rust , zig , or go . The MoonBit template builds a standalone service library with Bun, MoonBit (tested with v0.10.11), and a native C compiler. On Windows use an MSVC developer shell with cl or clang-cl and the Windows SDK. Set MOON , MOON_HOME , or CC to select tools. The provider itself needs neither Go nor the QuickGUI SDK; the included Go wrapper and demo show how another frontend can use it. Write service operations in native/extension.mbt : Inputs and successful replies are UTF-8 JSON bytes; errors are strings. Echoing the original bytes preserves nulls and large numbers. The adapter copies inputs into MoonBit-owned memory, checks the 64 KiB payload limit, emits the reply, and releases its native sink exactly once. Expected failures should return Err ; abort terminates the application. The build compiles MoonBit to C, then links a shared library with its own private runtime. Only the service descriptor is exported, so the provider can coexist with a MoonBit app and other providers. MoonBit's direct native backend does not yet produce shared-library packages ; this build path stays native and runs in the same process. Ordinary application edits reuse the built artifact. The generated adapter handles bounded synchronous operations on the application's UI worker. A nonblocking gate serializes runtime access, defers overlapping main-thread shutdown until the handler returns, and rejects concurrent or reentrant requests with a busy error. For slow native work or persistent sessions, extend the C adapter to copy input and retain the sink until completion. Workers must use the native reply/event callbacks and must not call MoonBit functions, retain the borrowed request context, or touch MoonBit-managed objects. Keep shutdown nonblocking. The manifest supplies the provider name, release version, and artifact package. Build through bun run build , and restart the demo after provider edits. --module sets the optional Go wrapper's module; edit native/moon.mod for the MoonBit provider module. moon -C native fmt formats the provider. The generated README covers the Go demo and local dependencies before publication. Implement the extension contract : versioned registration, method dispatch, asynchronous completion, and optional session events. No core integration is needed.

54.content: Directory paths are relative to the app project. The CLI reads quickgui.extension.json inside each directory; that manifest declares the provider name, version, and target artifacts. Build its library for each supported target. The CLI validates and packages explicitly selected providers and loads them before app startup. MoonBit does not discover extensions from Go imports.

56.content: Distribute a manifest, per-target native artifacts, and a MoonBit package exposing the service. The template stages the current host's library in artifacts/lib/<platform>-<arch>/ ; collect builds from each supported host and publish artifacts/ with its generated MoonBit license and notice. For direct executable runs, also declare @native.require_extension(name, version) before run and provide QUICKGUI_LIBRARY . Quick Git’s I/O extension demonstrates asynchronous process/file services. .bind_disabled(() => disabled.get()) changes actual native interaction state. A dimmed style alone does not disable a control. Use .property(@protocol.READ_ONLY, @protocol.Boolean(true)) for read-only input, and .property(@protocol.PLACEHOLDER, @protocol.Text("Name")) for a placeholder. Import egoist/quickgui/protocol for these constants. Use bind_style or native state styles for appearance, and the corresponding property for behavior.

.style(base).style(overrides) merges declarations in order; later properties win. .merge(other) does the same for style builders. Applying a style takes a snapshot. Changing the builder later does not update the mounted element. The compiler binds getter reads inside .style(...) and fluent modifiers. Later declarations keep precedence on every update; disappearing declarations are cleared or reveal an earlier fallback. Interaction-style callbacks can also read getters. Mutating an already-applied reusable builder is still a snapshot mutation, so derive styles from signals instead.

@native.command(json, callback) sends platform commands. @native.invoke(operation, params, callback) calls an asynchronous native service. Both callbacks receive Result[Json, String] . Use them for operations that need a response. @native.call is restricted to the core’s synchronous CPU-only allowlist. Callbacks belong to their registering owner. If an operation should survive the row or dialog that starts it, register it inside window.with_owner(() => { ... }) . Closing that window still retires the callback.

@native.on_event(kind, listener) subscribes in the current window context. @native.subscribe also returns a cancellation function. Use window=0 for application-level events. @native.watch_files(paths, changed, ready) uses OS file notifications and returns a stop function. These subscriptions are cleaned up with their owner. Persistent extension events use extension-event ; filter event.target to the session you opened. See Authoring Extensions .

@reactive.create_signal(initial) returns (read, write) . A call such as @ui.text("Count: \{count()}") is reactive when built with QuickGUI. The compiler also tracks expressions in button content, native properties, fluent styles, interaction styles, and child lists. Each binding updates its own retained nodes; the component does not rerun. Binding expressions must be pure. Ordinary setup remains ordinary MoonBit: let initial = count() captures a snapshot. Event handlers run only on events. Use @reactive.untrack(count) for an untracked read. Custom components keep normal parameter types: pass a getter when their input should stay live. Explicit bind_* methods and the lower-level Signal handle remain available for manual composition and keyed rows.

@reactive.memo(() => expression) returns a signal for a derived value. @reactive.create_effect tracks its actual reads, including conditional dependencies. @reactive.batch coalesces related writes. Avoid effects that rebuild an entire view to update one label. Components and dynamic branches own their subscriptions. Register teardown with @reactive.on_cleanup . Removing the owner retires its effects and callbacks; new windows have independent owners.

From the QuickGUI checkout, scaffold a provider: The command accepts moonbit , rust , zig , or go . The MoonBit template builds a standalone service library with Bun, MoonBit (tested with v0.10.11), and a native C compiler. On Windows use an MSVC developer shell with cl or clang-cl and the Windows SDK. Set MOON , MOON_HOME , or CC to select tools. The provider itself needs neither Go nor the QuickGUI SDK; the included Go wrapper and demo show how another frontend can use it. Write service operations in native/extension.mbt : Inputs and successful replies are UTF-8 JSON bytes; errors are strings. Echoing the original bytes preserves nulls and large numbers. The adapter copies inputs into MoonBit-owned memory, checks the 64 KiB payload limit, emits the reply, and releases its native sink exactly once. Expected failures should return Err ; abort terminates the application. The build compiles MoonBit to C, then links a shared library with its own private runtime. Only the service descriptor is exported, so the provider can coexist with a MoonBit app and other providers. MoonBit's direct native backend does not yet produce shared-library packages ; this build path stays native and runs in the same process. Ordinary application edits reuse the built artifact. The generated adapter handles bounded synchronous operations on the application's UI worker. A nonblocking gate serializes runtime access, defers overlapping main-thread shutdown until the handler returns, and rejects concurrent or reentrant requests with a busy error. For slow native work or persistent sessions, extend the C adapter to copy input and retain the sink until completion. Workers must use the native reply/event callbacks and must not call MoonBit functions, retain the borrowed request context, or touch MoonBit-managed objects. Keep shutdown nonblocking. The manifest supplies the provider name, release version, and artifact package. Build through bun run build , and restart the demo after provider edits. --module sets the optional Go wrapper's module; edit native/moon.mod for the MoonBit provider module. moon -C native fmt formats the provider. The generated README covers the Go demo and local dependencies before publication. This small table mounts all three rows: For large data, listen to .on_change(...) and retain its visibleRange field when present. Pass that field to @ui.visible_range(range, count) and mount only [start, end) with children_keyed . The end is exclusive; the initial range is bounded to 40 rows. Use .flex_row() , .flex_col() , .items_center() , and .justify_center() for common layouts. .flex(1) sets grow, shrink, and a zero basis. Give scrollable flex children .min_height(0) and a bounded parent size.

Use .hover(s => ...) , .active(s => ...) , and .focus_style(s => ...) for native pointer and focus states. .selected_style styles selected compound parts. These states are resolved by the native core. For a drop target’s drag-over appearance, use bind_json with @protocol.DRAG_OVER_STYLE and return a style’s .json() . Configure the node as a drop target as well; a style does not enable drop behavior. Import egoist/quickgui/protocol when using protocol constants. Add transitions to the base style to animate state changes.

Use @ui.rgb8(r, g, b) or @ui.rgba8(r, g, b, a) , with channels from 0 to 255. Window options accept these colors as JSON values; a raw integer uses 0xAABBGGRR ( 0 for transparent). Do not pass CSS color strings as a window’s background . @ui.svg(source) produces a mask tinted by .text_color(...) . For multiple graph colors, use separate tinted SVG layers, as shown in Quick Git.

Use @ui.window(component, options=...) to create a window; each window owns an independent tree. @native.current_window() is valid while building a component or handling a window callback. Capture that handle for later .close() or .focus() calls. Creation is asynchronous. Wait for window-ready-to-show before querying native geometry or state. Set show: false to prepare a hidden window. Options use the native JSON schema, including title , width , height , background , titleBarStyle , trafficLightX , and trafficLightY .

Use Checkbox , Switch , Select and the other control pages in the sidebar. Their helpers wire native roles, values and scope. Read-only and disabled controls suppress default changes; Event.prevent_default() can cancel an application event without removing component behavior.

Use MoonBit primitives, native table parts, and resizable panels. MoonBit provides the same native component families as Go, using child lists and fluent styles, properties, and event handlers. The sidebar includes the full component reference and macOS SwiftUI hosts.

Use quickgui check and quickgui test so tests receive the same view transform as builds. Add --release for release-backend tests. Raw moon check checks the original types, while raw moon test bypasses implicit view bindings. The CLI preserves source files and maps compiler diagnostics, assertion failures, and symbolicated stack locations back to them. Native debugger breakpoints and stepping currently use the generated files in .quickgui/moonbit-sources ; original-file breakpoint mapping is not supported yet. Editor completion and type checking continue to use ordinary MoonBit.

Use quickgui keygen --sparkle to create signing keys and keep the private key outside the repository. Build with quickgui build , then publish the generated appcast and signed release archive at the configured download location.
Use router.link(path, label) for a navigation link. router.navigate(path) pushes history; pass replace=true to replace the current entry. router.go(-1) goes back and router.go(1) goes forward.
Use swift_ui_quickgui_host_view(render, width=..., height=...) to build a QuickGUI subtree inside SwiftUI. The callback creates nodes in the embedded view’s own window.
